logline: A national shooting champion transfers to her dead twin brother's school refusing to accept the suicide verdict, and teams up with a scarred loner who secretly punishes bullies - uncovering a conspiracy of cruelty that runs deeper than either anticipated.

renewal.note: Twelve-episode series concluded on Disney+ in December 2022. No renewal announced; series tells a self-contained story.

bollymeter.basis: Critics and audiences agreed this was among Disney+ Korea's strongest originals - praised for young lead performances by Shin Ye-eun and Lomon, a socially engaged script about school bullying and institutional failure, and propulsive mystery plotting that sustained tension across twelve episodes.

seasons.review_body: Revenge of Others arrived on Disney+ in November 2022 as one of the platform's strongest early Korean originals. Directed by Kim Yoo-jin and written by Lee Hee-myung, the show centred on a topical social issue - school bullying and the systemic silencing of its victims - framed as a mystery thriller rather than a didactic drama. Shin Ye-eun and Lomon anchored the show: a driven shooting champion investigating her twin brother's death, and a financially struggling student who doles out vigilante justice to protect the vulnerable. Audience reception was warm, with an IMDb score of 7.6. Korean drama communities cited it as a tightly plotted, emotionally engaged entry in the school-mystery genre. No Rotten Tomatoes aggregate was available at the time of writing; the IMDb score and sustained viewer engagement are the clearest available indicators of the show's quality.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets up Chan-mi's grief and scepticism with precision - the twin bond is established economically before the mystery hook arrives. The school environment is rendered with the particular cruelty of Korean elite-high social dynamics, and the show immediately signals it intends to take its subject seriously.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Chan-mi learns the details of her brother's death and decides the official account cannot be trusted - a quiet, devastating pivot.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the conspiracy with satisfying clarity, paying off twelve episodes of slow-burn investigation. The emotional cost lands because the show built its characters carefully - the resolution feels earned rather than mechanical.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The truth about the events that killed Chan-mi's brother is laid bare - the institutional complicity that made it possible is the show's sharpest moral argument.
